hints: In an AP, $T_1 + T_5 = 2T_3 \implies 2\cos x + 10\cos x = 2(-6\sqrt{3}\sin x)$.
Find the exact angle in $\frac{\pi}{2} < x < \pi$.
walkthrough:
Use the arithmetic progression relation $T_1 + T_5 = 2T_3$ for the given terms:
$$2\cos x + 10\cos x = 2(-6\sqrt{3}\sin x) \implies 12\cos x = -12\sqrt{3}\sin x$$

Rearrange into a single trigonometric ratio:
$$\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = -\frac{12}{12\sqrt{3}} \implies \tan x = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$$

Identify the unique angle in the second quadrant domain $\frac{\pi}{2} < x < \pi$:
$$x = \pi - \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{5\pi}{6}$$

ai_rubric.Arithmetic Progressions: Forms $12\cos x = -12\sqrt{3}\sin x$ (M1). Solves for $\tan x = -1/\sqrt{3}$ (DM1). Obtains exact value $x = \frac{5\pi}{6}$ (A1).

hints: Evaluate first term $a = 2\cos(5\pi/6) = -\sqrt{3}$ and common difference $d = -\sqrt{3}$.
Apply $S_{25} = \frac{25}{2}[2a + 24d]$ and state the exact radical.
walkthrough:
Evaluate the first term $a$ and common difference $d$ at $x = \frac{5\pi}{6}$:
$$a = 2\cos\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}\right) = 2\left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = -\sqrt{3}$$
$$T_3 = -6\sqrt{3}\sin\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}\right) = -6\sqrt{3}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = -3\sqrt{3}$$
$$2d = T_3 - T_1 = -3\sqrt{3} - (-\sqrt{3}) = -2\sqrt{3} \implies d = -\sqrt{3}$$

Calculate the sum of the first $25$ terms using $S_n = \frac{n}{2}[2a + (n - 1)d]$:
$$S_{25} = \frac{25}{2}[2(-\sqrt{3}) + 24(-\sqrt{3})] = \frac{25}{2}[-26\sqrt{3}] = 25(-13\sqrt{3}) = -325\sqrt{3}$$

ai_rubric.Arithmetic Progressions: Finds common difference $d = -\sqrt{3}$ (B1 FT). Applies sum formula with $n=25$ (M1). Obtains exact sum $-325\sqrt{3}$ (A1).
